conclusions: Node StreamBase::AddAccessor constructs two FunctionTemplate records with the original Signature, constructor behavior kThrow and distinct getter/setter side-effect metadata. It installs those templates with ObjectTemplate::SetAccessorProperty. onread is DontDelete|DontEnum; ordinary data-property shadowing of onread is independent of StreamBase's internal field.

ApiNatives::DefineAccessorProperty preserves FunctionTemplateInfo components when BreakAtEntry is false. The actual debug break branch separately materializes and installs the DebugBreakTrampoline. No blanket eager-JSFunction claim is made.

Object::GetPropertyWithAccessor and Object::SetPropertyWithAccessor recognize the unmaterialized FunctionTemplateInfo and invoke Builtins::InvokeApiFunction directly after switching to the holder's creation context. The setter supplies the one actual value and returns normal assignment success after a completed native invocation. This path does not call AccessorPair::GetComponent.

GetOwnPropertyDescriptor materializes the getter first and setter second through AccessorPair::GetComponent using the holder's native context. GetComponent instantiates a FunctionTemplateInfo via ToHandleChecked, replaces that component with the actual JSFunction and returns it; subsequent component reads return the cached actual value. This is a distinct allocation/native-failure boundary from ordinary property access.

BaseObject's actual internal-field getter and setter use the converted/signature-admitted args.This() object. The setter checks Value::IsFunction with native CHECK before writing the field. Neither body unwraps the native BaseObject pointer, so clearing native State during realm cleanup alone does not remove the wrapper's internal onread value.

The completed Registry StreamFields owner supplies the traced onread edge and detached-wrapper lifetime, but it does not supply this public lazy native accessor/template mechanism. Installing eager native ModuleCallable getter/setter objects would add real early JS allocations and therefore is not silently used as a substitute.
